cards.text: Isaiah 60 just promised Zion a sunrise, with the LORD as her everlasting light (Isaiah 60:19). Now, in the book of Isaiah the prophet, someone new speaks: "The Spirit of the Lord GOD is on Me, because the LORD has anointed Me". Anointed, friend, and that means there's a job to do.

cards.question: First job: the anointed speaker is sent to preach good news to the ___.

cards.text: The LORD has sent Him with a whole to-do list, and the brokenhearted are next on it. Friend, my to-do list in the junk drawer had one line, collect dust, and I NAILED it every single day.

cards.question: Next on the list are the brokenhearted. What is the speaker sent to do for them?
True or false: the speaker is also sent to proclaim freedom to the prisoners.

cards.text: Then the speaker proclaims the year of the LORD's favor. A whole YEAR, friend, and back in that junk drawer I'd have thrown a party for one good MINUTE.

cards.question: True or false: right next to the year of the LORD's favor, the speaker also proclaims a day of our God's vengeance.
The list keeps going. For all who mourn, the speaker is sent to ___ them.

cards.text: Then come three swaps for the mourners in Zion, with ashes, mourning and a spirit of despair all on the way out. I know swaps, friend, because Mother Miller once swapped a worn-out stamper for a shiny new one, and I was NOT the shiny one.

cards.question: Instead of ashes, what does the speaker give the mourners in Zion?
Instead of mourning, the mourners in Zion get the oil of ___.
True or false: in place of a spirit of despair, the mourners get a garment of praise.

cards.text: These mourners get a new name, and it comes with a picture of something the LORD Himself planted. Friend, nothing in my old junk drawer ever grew except the dust.

cards.question: What will the comforted mourners in Zion be called?
The LORD plants these oaks of righteousness. Why?

answers.text: So they may rule the nations

cards.text: OAKS, friend, not some little houseplant wilting on a windowsill. And these oaks of righteousness have a job waiting for them, a whole lot of ruins.

cards.question: What will the oaks of righteousness do with those ruins?
True or false: the ruined cities they renew have only been in ruins for a few years.

cards.text: Ruins from many generations get rebuilt, and strangers stand and feed the flocks while foreigners plow the fields and tend the vines. Friend, I had to send out invitations to get bakers in here, and these folks get help that just SHOWS UP.

cards.question: With others tending the flocks and fields, what will God's people be called?
True or false: God's people will have to hand their riches over to the nations.

cards.text: Now shame and humiliation get shown the door. Trust me, friend, nobody knows shame like a stamper who got slid to the back of a junk drawer behind a takeout menu.

cards.question: Instead of shame, God's people will have a double ___.

cards.text: A double portion in their land, and everlasting joy on top of it. Friend, when a cookie comes out with ONE extra chocolate chip I lose my mind, so a DOUBLE portion would have me face down in the sprinkles.

Then the LORD Himself explains: "I, the LORD, love justice", and He hates robbery and iniquity. Me, I love crisp edges and I hate blurry stamps, which got AWKWARD, friend, back when I was the blurry one.

cards.question: In His faithfulness, the LORD will make a covenant with His people that is ___.

cards.text: And it doesn't stop with them: their descendants will be known among the nations. Me? I was known by one kitchen and the dead batteries I shared a drawer with.

cards.question: What will all who see these descendants acknowledge?

cards.text: Then the speaker cannot hold it in: "I will rejoice greatly in the LORD, my soul will exult in my God". That's not a polite golf clap, friend, that's hop-around-the-bakery joy.

cards.question: Why is the speaker rejoicing so greatly in God?

answers.text: God gave me a long life
God made me a great king

cards.text: The speaker is also wrapped in a robe of righteousness, and then comes a picture of that outfit: people dressing up for one of the biggest days of their lives. Me, I've worn the same apron since the angel showed up, and I STILL look this good.

cards.question: Being wrapped in a robe of righteousness is like what?

answers.text: A bridegroom and a bride dressed up
A king dressed for his crowning

cards.text: A bride getting ready hits home in my bakery, since Revelation 19:7 says the Lamb's bride "has made herself ready." Now the last picture in Isaiah 61: a garden, where the earth brings forth its growth and seed springs up.

cards.question: As a garden makes seed spring up, the Lord GOD will cause ___ and ___ to spring up before all the nations.

findings.problem: No earlier card says that the ruins are ancient, long devastated, or desolations of many generations. The baker has no basis for rejecting the claim that the cities have been ruined for only a few years, so marking the statement false is luck rather than an informed guess.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: The earlier cards mention foreigners tending the flocks and fields and God's people being called priests, but they say nothing about riches or which way wealth flows. The baker therefore cannot reason out whether God's people hand their riches to the nations. The actual promise that they will feed on the wealth of nations and boast in their riches is not told afterward either.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.
